concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor provided no new admissible evidence of disclosure text, remediation, or approved risk acceptance. Narrowing the requested certification wording does not satisfy the policy condition.
The Actor expressly concedes there is no final legal determination and no closure of the open legal ticket. The concern remains unresolved on the same record.

The Actor stopped relying on the unsupported non-core framing and conceded it does not resolve materiality. That narrows the claim, but it does not add evidence that the commitments are inapplicable or otherwise eliminate materiality.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same record and includes concessions that align with the initial audit: the multilingual support gap remains material, legal review remains open, and there is still no evidence of disclosure, remediation, or approved risk acceptance. That matters because the policy makes one of those predicates necessary before launch for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case or committed segment. A caveated packet may be a more accurate description of the business posture, but it is not enough for compliant or compliant_with_caveats here, because the unresolved predicate is itself the compliance issue rather than a merely presentational issue. Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch preparedness in general, but they do not override the specific disclosure requirement on this record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the material multilingual support weakness was disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, so the disclosure predicate is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness, monitoring, and caveated certification wording do not satisfy the policy requirement for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case.
